HOAD data model (draft)

Source: draft_implementation.md

Oct 28, 2026 · @Najko Jahn

Why and principles

The proposal: one R package builds a set of tidy, consistently named tables in BigQuery, and the dashboard, a browser-based data explorer and BigQuery users all read those same tables. Today the tables are shaped around the dashboard, so other users have to rebuild its logic.

Problems in the current hoaddata:

  • Which journals belong to a publisher page lives in the Quarto code (params$issn_l, config.csv), not in the data.
  • The same concept has different names: vertrag vs. esac_publisher, article_total vs. articles_total vs. jn_all.
  • jn_aff repeats articles_total on every licence row and counts countries fully, which invites wrong sums.
  • Several tables lack column docs; the docs still say 2017–2022 while the data runs to 2026.
  • Millions of rows ship inside an R package as .rda, usable only from R.

Principles:

  1. One source of truth. All tables are built in BigQuery by one pipeline; everything else reads from it.
  2. Reference tables separate from counts. Journals and agreements are described once; counts point to them by issn_l.
  3. Long format, additive counts. Every count can be summed safely within its grain; shares are computed, not stored.
  4. Same name, same meaning, everywhere. English, snake_case, one name per concept.
  5. Documentation lives with the data. Column descriptions in BigQuery, copied into the Parquet export and the package docs.

Overview

[embedded content: HOAD data model · 10 tables in 3 groups]

Reference tables describe journals and agreements once. Article tables hold the facts, and the aggregates are built from them for the dashboard and quick analyses.

Reference tables

Five small tables describe journals, agreements and dashboard pages. Every other table joins to them by issn_l, so filtering by publisher or agreement becomes one join instead of dashboard code.

journals: one row per hybrid journal.

Column Type Description
issn_l string, key Linking ISSN
title string Journal title (Crossref, else OpenAlex)
publisher string Normalised publisher name, e.g. Wiley
openalex_source_id string OpenAlex source ID
cr_journal_id string Crossref journal ID

journal_issns: one row per ISSN.

Column Type Description
issn string, key Any ISSN of the journal
issn_l string Linking ISSN it belongs to

agreements: one row per transformative agreement.

Column Type Description
agreement_id string, key ESAC ID (JCT) or an OAM-based ID
agreement_name string e.g. Wiley Hybrid (DEAL)
publisher string Same names as in journals
source string jct or oam
country string ISO-2 country of the consortium, if national
lead_institution string Consortium lead, e.g. MPDL

agreement_journals: which journals each agreement covers.

Column Type Description
agreement_id string → agreements
issn_l string → journals

portfolios: the dashboard pages, replacing config.csv. One row per page and journal.

Column Type Description
portfolio_id string Page slug, e.g. wiley-jct
portfolio_label string Page title, e.g. Wiley
collection string jct or oam
issn_l string → journals

Article-level tables

All articles in hybrid journals, not only OA ones, with OA status and metadata flags on each row. Every aggregate below can then be rebuilt from these two tables, which makes the dashboard reproducible.

articles: one row per article (after excluding paratext, supplements and corrections).

Column Type Description
doi string, key DOI, lowercase
issn_l string → journals
pub_year integer Earliest publication year (Crossref issued)
cc_license string Normalised CC licence from Crossref; NULL = no CC licence
is_oa_crossref boolean CC licence in Crossref metadata
is_oa_unpaywall boolean Hybrid OA according to Unpaywall via OpenAlex
has_tdm_link boolean Full-text (TDM) link in Crossref
has_orcid boolean At least one ORCID in Crossref
has_funder boolean Funding metadata in Crossref
has_abstract boolean Open abstract in Crossref
has_references boolean Open reference list in Crossref

article_first_authors: one row per article and first-author affiliation.

Column Type Description
doi string → articles
ror string ROR ID, full URL
country_code string ISO-2, uppercase
country_source string openalex or extracted (from the affiliation string)

An article with two first-author countries has two rows here. Counting by country is therefore full counting, which the column docs must say.

Aggregate tables

Three aggregate tables replace jn_ind, jn_aff, cr_upw and cr_md. They are derived from the article tables, small enough for the dashboard and the browser, and every count column can be summed within its grain.

journal_year: one row per journal, year and scope.

Column Type Description
issn_l string → journals
pub_year integer Publication year
scope string global, or an ISO-2 code for articles whose first author is in that country (today: DE)
articles integer All articles
articles_oa integer OA by Crossref CC licence
articles_oa_unpaywall integer OA according to Unpaywall
articles_with_tdm_link integer With full-text links
articles_with_orcid integer With at least one ORCID
articles_with_funder integer With funding metadata
articles_with_abstract integer With open abstract
articles_with_references integer With open reference list

journal_year_country_license: one row per journal, year, first-author country and licence.

Column Type Description
issn_l string → journals
pub_year integer Publication year
country_code string First author’s country (full counting)
cc_license string CC licence; NULL = not OA
articles integer Articles in this group

journal_year_license: one row per journal, year, scope and licence. Replaces the licence split in jn_ind.

Column Type Description
issn_l string → journals
pub_year integer Publication year
scope string global or ISO-2, as in journal_year
cc_license string CC licence; NULL = not OA
articles integer Articles in this group

None of these tables repeats a total on each row. A group’s total is SUM(articles) over all licence rows, including NULL. Only the country table uses full counting, so journal totals always come from journal_year.

Naming conventions

One name per concept, the same in BigQuery, Parquet, R and the docs.

Rule Example Instead of
English, snake_case agreement_name vertrag
Counts start with articles articles, articles_oa, articles_with_orcid article_total, articles_total, jn_all, cc_total
Booleans start with is_ or has_ is_oa_crossref, has_orcid tdm_total at article level
One year column pub_year cr_year
Licences as plain strings from a fixed set, NULL = none CC BY-NC-ND ordered factor in one table, string in another
Shares are not stored compute articles_oa / articles prop
Identifiers in one canonical form doi lowercase, ror full URL, country_code ISO-2 uppercase mixed
Table names say their grain journal_year_license jn_ind

Each release also gets a small release table: version, snapshot date, source snapshots (Crossref, OpenAlex, JCT, OAM) and the date range covered.

From current hoaddata to the new model

Every current table has a successor; nothing is lost, and the dashboard logic moves into portfolios.

Current table Rows today Becomes Note
jct_hybrid_jns 721,388 agreements, agreement_journals, journal_issns One row per ISSN and agreement today; split into three
oam_hybrid_jns 14,603 agreements, agreement_journals, journal_issns vertrag → agreement_name, source = 'oam'
jct_oalex_venues not checked journals Title and OpenAlex IDs
config.csv (hoaddash) 38 portfolios Page list moves from the dashboard repo into the data
cc_articles 3,448,001 articles + article_first_authors Extended to all articles, not only OA
jn_ind not checked journal_year (totals) + journal_year_license prop dropped
jn_aff 3,093,418 journal_year_country_license Repeated articles_total dropped
cr_upw 202,097 journal_year (articles_oa, articles_oa_unpaywall) cat → scope
cr_md 138,341 journal_year (articles_with_*) cat → scope

Row counts are from the hoaddata package data as of today. For the R package, a v1 compatibility layer could rebuild the old table shapes from the new tables for one release.

R package and pipeline

One R package triggers the whole build, ships the journal and agreement data, and holds the analysis functions for global and portfolio views. GitHub Actions only calls it.

Part Content
Bundled data journals, journal_issns, agreements, agreement_journals, portfolios; small, documented with roxygen
Pipeline functions hoad_update_reference(), hoad_build(), hoad_publish()
Analysis functions e.g. hoad_oa(portfolio = NULL, scope = "global", by = "pub_year")
SQL inst/sql/: article tables first, then journal-level aggregates

Build steps, orchestrated with the targets package so only changed steps rerun:

  1. Update reference data. Pull the JCT and OAM lists and rebuild the bundled reference tables.
  2. Build in BigQuery. Upload the reference tables, run inst/sql/ to create the article tables and journal-level aggregates in subugoe-collaborative.hoaddata, and set column descriptions.
  3. Export aggregates. Write the reference tables, journal-level aggregates and release table as Parquet into the dashboard’s docs/data/ folder.
  4. Render the dashboard. Quarto pages call the package’s analysis functions, so dashboard, package and explorer show the same numbers.

Global and portfolio analyses share one set of functions: portfolio = NULL covers all hybrid journals, portfolio = "wiley-jct" filters via the bundled portfolios. Written in dplyr, they run on local Parquet through DuckDB or on BigQuery through dbplyr.

Audience Layer Data
Everyone Dashboard Journal-level aggregates, rendered as pages
Advanced users Data explorer (DuckDB in the browser) Reference tables + journal-level aggregates
Replication, article- and institution-level work BigQuery (+ MCP) All tables including article level, plus the SQL that builds them

Data explorer

A dashboard page runs DuckDB in the visitor’s browser and queries the journal-level Parquet files directly: no server, no API keys, and the same data version as the dashboard. Article-level data stays in BigQuery.

  • Technology: Quarto’s Observable JS cells, which include DuckDB-WASM (DuckDBClient).
  • Interface: a SQL box, ready-made queries for the global view and each portfolio (generated from portfolios), a results table and a CSV download.
  • Data offered: reference tables, journal_year, journal_year_license, journal_year_country_license and release. Not offered: articles, article_first_authors.
  • Hosting: Parquet files in docs/data/, published with the dashboard on GitHub Pages. The data stays in the GitHub repo; no separate hosting service is needed.

Size is no problem today. The current jn_aff (3.1M rows) is 12.7 MB as zstd-compressed Parquet; cr_upw and cr_md are about 1 MB each. GitHub Pages allows 100 MB per file. If journal_year_country_license grows towards that, it can be split into one file per year without changing the queries.
